stories.title: Vocal divergence accompanies auditory and neural changes in urban Eurasian tree sparrows
stories.description: Urbanization elevates chronic anthropogenic noise that can mask acoustic communication, yet changes in vocal signals, auditory reception, and neural processing are rarely examined together. Here, we compared urban and rural populations of Eurasian tree sparrows (Passer montanus) in Shijiazhuang, China, integrating vocal acoustics, auditory brainstem responses (ABRs), external and inner-ear morphology, adult neurogenesis, and proteomic profiles of the caudomedial nidopallium (NCM). Urban and rural birds differed markedly in syllable composition, with only a subset of syllable types shared between habitats. Shared syllable types also showed syllable-specific acoustic differences between habitats, including higher peak frequencies and intensities in several urban syllable types. In parallel, urban birds exhibited selective reductions in ABR amplitudes, smaller ear apertures, and altered cochlear hair cell organization. At the neural level, urban birds showed evidence of reduced adult neurogenesis in both the lateral ventricle and NCM, alongside proteomic changes associated with stress responses, synaptic organization, and neuronal development. Together, these co-occurring patterns suggest that potential vocal compensation may be accompanied by sensory and neural constraints, although their consequences for signal perception and communication success remain untested. These findings highlight the importance of examining signal production, auditory reception, and neural processing together when evaluating responses to urban environments.

stories.title: Median-pi-sigma artificial neural network for time series forecasting
stories.description: This study proposes a novel robust artificial neural network architecture, called the Median–Pi-Sigma Neural Network, for time series forecasting problems. Unlike conventional neural network approaches that rely primarily on additive neuron structures and external robustness techniques, the proposed architecture incorporates robustness directly into the computational structure of the network. In the proposed model, a median-based hidden layer is employed to suppress the propagation of anomalous observations and reduce the sensitivity of the network to noise. To compensate for the potential loss of representational capability caused by median processing, a second hidden layer composed of multiplicative product-unit neurons is integrated into the architecture. This hybrid structure enables the model to simultaneously achieve robustness and high-order nonlinear representation capability within a unified framework. Due to the non-differentiable nature of the median operator and the highly nonlinear error surface generated by multiplicative neurons, the network parameters are optimized using a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The forecasting performance of the proposed architecture was evaluated using ten different Financial Times Stock Exchange (FTSE) time series datasets and compared with several important neural network models in the literature, including multilayer perceptron, Pi-Sigma, multiplicative neuron, recurrent, gated recurrent neural network, long short-term memory deep artificial neural network, and dendritic neural network architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Median Pi Neural Network achieved the lowest average RMSE values in many of the datasets and generally outperformed competing methods in terms of forecasting accuracy and robustness. Statistical analyses based on the Friedman test further confirmed the superiority of the proposed approach. The findings indicate that integrating median-based robustness with multiplicative nonlinear modelling provides an effective and powerful framework for financial time series forecasting under noisy environments.

stories.title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals novel stem cell markers for corneal limbal epithelium homeostasis
stories.description: Sox9 is a well-established marker of skin epithelial hair follicle stem cells and has been observed in the corneal limbus of Sox9-EGFP transgenic mice. Using Sox9-EGFP as a reference marker, this study characterized the transcriptomic atlas of corneal limbal epithelial cells during homeostasis and identified novel markers of limbal stem cells (LSCs) by single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). A total of 20,351 viable cells were profiled, revealing 13 distinct cell clusters with unique molecular signatures. The cluster enriched with EGFP-positive cells was identified as the putative LSCs population during corneal epithelial homeostasis. Comparative analysis of corneal LSCs and early differentiated cells revealed several differentially expressed genes (DEGs) strongly associated with stemness-related pathways, including Gabrp, Fmo1, Fmo2, and Alcam, which were identified as potential novel LSC markers. Among these DEGs, Gabrp, and Alcam were exclusively expressed in the limbus, as confirmed by quantitative PCR (qPCR), Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. This study delineated the heterogeneous cellular composition of the limbal epithelium and uncovered several novel candidate markers that may be critical for maintaining corneal epithelial homeostasis.
